12jcoxm: Y, o, pero: adding, choosing, contrasting
1f6oo5o: **Y** adds two things or two ideas: _Hablo español **y** portugués_. **O** gives an option: _¿Vienes el sábado **o** el domingo?_ **Pero** introduces a contrast or a difficulty: _Me gusta el proyecto, **pero** no tengo mucho tiempo_.
1oq2xqz: Before **pero** you almost always write a **comma**. Before **y** and **o**, in a simple list, you don't.
yekaoz: To sound right, **y** changes to **e** before a word that starts with the _i_ sound (**i-**, **hi-**): _madre **e** hija_, _francés **e** inglés_. And **o** changes to **u** before the _o_ sound (**o-**, **ho-**): _siete **u** ocho_, _mujeres **u** hombres_.
1rj1fp2: Listen to the next word: if it starts with the same sound (_y-i_, _o-o_), change the connector.
1hosj7b: To say **no** to two things, use **no + verb + … ni …**: _No tengo coche **ni** moto_. The first _no_ goes before the verb, as in any negative sentence.
1ttcy6s: Don't say _no… y…_ for two negative things: _No hablo alemán **ni** ruso_, not _No hablo alemán y ruso_.
132edif: It also works with two verbs: _Los domingos **no** trabajo **ni** estudio_.
13g8x8u: To ask for the **reason**, you say **¿Por qué…?**: two words and an accent on _qué_. To answer, you say **porque**: one word, no accent.
y6vn16: After **porque** comes a clause with a **conjugated verb**: _Quiero ayudar **porque** me gustan los niños_. _Llego tarde **porque** hay mucho tráfico_.
1mptkrc: To give your opinion before the reason you can use **creo que** + clause: _**Creo que** es un buen proyecto **porque** ayuda a las familias_.
ms7jew: To **ask**: two words and an accent, **por qué**.
9bqhmf: To say the **goal** of an action, you use **para + infinitive** (the unconjugated verb in -ar, -er, -ir): _Estudio español **para hablar** con mis vecinos_.
1efh4z9: The question is **¿Para qué…?**: _¿Para qué necesitas el diccionario?_ — _**Para traducir** un cuento_.
4ha465: Compare: **porque** looks at the cause, what comes first (_porque tengo tiempo libre_); **para** looks at the goal, what you want to achieve (_para aprender algo nuevo_). After **para**, never a conjugated verb.
1j792xx: Trick: if you can put _para conseguir_ (in order to get) in front, it's **para**; if you can put _la razón es que_ (the reason is that), it's **porque**.
1x08sk3: After **para**, the verb is in the **infinitive**.
ob7r9p: It's a goal with an infinitive: **para ayudar**.

19elao: **¿Por qué?** and **porque** are written differently and they also sound different. In the question, the stress is on **qué**: _por-**QUÉ**_. In the answer, the stress is on **por**: _**POR**-que_.
1wn6vmi: The question _¿Por qué…?_ usually falls at the end, like all questions with a question word. The answer _porque…_ runs on with no pause up to the verb: _porque-tengo-tiempo_.
ma7r0b: The connectors **y**, **e**, **o**, **u** are weak and blend with the words around them: _pan y queso_ sounds like _pa-ni-que-so_; _siete u ocho_ sounds like _sie-teu-o-cho_.
4rmm9b: Four forms to spell correctly: **¿por qué?** (question, two words, accent), **porque** (answer, one word), **para qué** (question about the goal) and **para** + infinitive (answer).
1cp0s1u: Stress on _qué_: _por-QUÉ_. Your voice falls at the end.
